candidates.title: Depin a Mini-Fit Jr. 5556 terminal from a 5557 housing
candidates.objective: With a de-energized four-circuit Mini-Fit Jr. 39012040/5557 receptacle fixed in a service fixture, guide the HT60630B extraction tool around the selected 5556 terminal, depress both locking tangs, maintain tool engagement, push the wire toward the tool if needed, and then pull the wire and terminal from the rear without releasing neighboring terminals or damaging the reusable housing.
skills: precision tool-tip alignment with housing guide slots
constrained dual-blade insertion around a recessed contact
contact and force control while depressing two locking tangs
bimanual coordination between sustained tool engagement and opposite-side wire pull
regrasping a slender tool and wire
avoidance of neighboring terminals and housing walls
candidates.success_conditions: Research-stage rubric: the designated terminal and its wire must exit through the rear of its original cavity through robot-applied contact forces; the housing stays fixed and reusable; all other terminals remain fully retained; the wire remains attached to the extracted terminal; and the tool, housing, insulation, contact body, and adjacent terminals show no prohibited displacement or damage. Success must persist for 3 seconds after both grippers release the extracted terminal and tool. Score zero for extracting the wrong or an additional terminal, pulling the wire out of its crimp, breaking or permanently displacing the housing, bypassing the tangs, or teleporting/welding/state-overwriting the terminal. Partial credit may distinguish correct tool entry, both tangs depressed, and partial rearward withdrawal, but no unmeasured numerical force or damage threshold is asserted. Development is blocked until the rigid tang/contact abstraction passes insertion, retention, overload, and reset tests with measured proxy hardware.
candidates.industrial_value: Molex identifies HT60630B as tooling specifically designed to extract crimped Mini-Fit terminals, while TE identifies terminal extraction without housing damage as important to OEM and aftermarket rework and repair. Molex also lists Mini-Fit connectors for commercial-cleaning-robot drive and motion-control interconnects. This supports harness rework as an industrial manipulation objective, without claiming that every 39012040 housing is installed in that particular robot application.
candidates.dexterity: High but feasible. The robot must enter narrow housing slots with two blades outside the contact, recognize terminal contact, maintain tang-depressing engagement, optionally unload the tangs by pushing the wire forward, and coordinate an opposing gentle pull. This is materially different from mating a completed connector or operating its external latch.

candidates.asset_plan: Use the documented four-circuit 39012040/5557 housing and a compatible 5556 terminal only; do not mix the 5378 geometry or another extraction-tool series. Build dimensioned rigid housing, terminal, crimp barrel, wire, and HT60630B proxy meshes from the acquired Molex drawing plus measurements of reference parts. Represent each terminal tang as a constrained articulated rigid leaf with calibrated detent and irreversible damage state rather than a deformable solver. The wire may initially be a short rigid handle for component-physics tests; any later segmented cable must use an already validated YAM-compatible model. Validate blade clearance, outside-contact guidance, tang release, retained-state pull resistance, extraction after release, neighbor retention, overload damage, and reset repeatability before attempting a full robot demo in pinned Isaac Sim 6.1.0/YAM 0059d02a1a91bc6834c1d0846022891df0c78730. No task object may be teleported or welded to produce extraction.
candidates.risk: Medium-high implementation risk. The acquired sources establish procedure, pitch, compatible families, intended tooling, and terminal non-reusability, but do not provide blade thickness, tang stiffness, release force, pull-out force, or allowable housing-load limits. Those values require measured reference hardware. The catalog text screen found no direct depin/terminal-extraction objective, but this is not conclusive semantic proof; the complete accepted, pending, open, team, and benchmark comparison must be repeated after the objective and physics are implemented.

candidates.title: Extract a 5378-series terminal with a single HT60630B blade
candidates.objective: Hold the compatible housing with its locking tab upward, bend the wire down, insert one HT60630B blade beneath the locking tab, and pull the wire and tool together to remove the terminal.
skills: single-blade insertion beneath a recessed tab
coordinated same-direction tool and wire pull
candidates.success_conditions: The selected 5378 terminal exits its cavity through robot-applied blade and pulling forces while the housing remains intact and no neighboring terminal is released. Zero for bypassing the locking tab, wire/crimp separation, housing damage, unintended extraction, or state overwrite. Exact force and damage thresholds remain blocked pending measurements.
candidates.industrial_value: Molex provides an explicit manufacturer procedure for extracting individual 5378 terminals with this tool, establishing a real connector-service operation.
candidates.dexterity: High. Unlike the selected dual-blade process, this sequence requires wire bending, insertion of one blade beneath a specific tab, and simultaneous withdrawal of the wire and tool.

candidates.asset_plan: Acquire the authoritative 5378 housing and terminal drawings and reference hardware before modeling. Use rigid PhysX geometry and an articulated locking tab calibrated from the actual parts. Validate wire-bending clearance, tab release, simultaneous pull, damage modes, and YAM reachability before full-demo work.
candidates.risk: Not selected. It is meaningfully different in contact mechanics from the dual-blade 5556 procedure, but the acquired package lacks a 5378 housing drawing, selected part number, complete geometry, and robot-application evidence. It also shares the broader depinning objective, so it offers weaker novelty separation than the selected, better-specified four-circuit Mini-Fit Jr. setup.

candidates.title: Non-destructively extract a reusable harness terminal for OEM rework
candidates.objective: Identify a specified harness cavity, insert the connector-specific extraction tool, release the internal retention feature, and remove the terminal while preserving both terminal and housing for inspected reuse.
candidates.success_conditions: The correct terminal is removed by the specified tool; both terminal and housing pass geometry and retention inspections defined by the selected manufacturer's service specification; adjacent terminals remain retained. Zero for wrong-tool use, terminal or housing damage, wire pull-out, unintended release, or state overwrite. This objective is blocked because no acquired source supplies a complete compatible part/tool set, procedure, reuse inspection, or numerical acceptance limits.
candidates.industrial_value: TE explicitly states that avoiding terminal or housing damage is important for OEM and aftermarket rework and repair, so the objective has real industrial value.
candidates.dexterity: Potentially high because success depends on releasing an internal feature while keeping two reusable parts undamaged, but difficulty cannot be specified credibly until a concrete connector and tool are chosen.

candidates.asset_plan: Do not build from the generic TE page. First acquire one manufacturer procedure, exact tool identifier, terminal and housing drawings, reuse policy, inspection criteria, and measured reference hardware. Only then construct and validate rigid contact, retention, and damage physics.
candidates.risk: Blocked and not selected. The available evidence establishes industrial relevance but not an executable equipment-specific procedure or geometry. It would be invalid to invent a connector, release mechanism, force threshold, or reuse criterion.

candidates.title: Replace a drive-and-motion-control connector in a commercial cleaning robot
candidates.objective: Remove a failed motion-control harness connector and install its replacement while preserving surrounding wiring and seals.
candidates.success_conditions: Blocked: no defensible success rubric can be written from the acquired sources because they do not identify a cleaning-robot assembly, connector part number, access geometry, removal procedure, insertion procedure, or sealing inspection.
candidates.industrial_value: Molex documents that commercial cleaning-robot motors and motion systems require reliable power and signal connectors in demanding environments, establishing the subsystem's industrial importance.
candidates.dexterity: Potentially high, but currently unsubstantiated for any actual equipment geometry.

candidates.risk: Blocked and not selected. The source proves application relevance only; treating it as an assembly or service instruction would invent the task geometry and procedure.

selection_reason: This is the only candidate that combines a manufacturer-specified manipulation sequence, an exact extraction tool, a concrete four-circuit housing family with 4.20 mm pitch, rigid-body-compatible contact mechanics, and evidence for industrial rework relevance. It requires internal tang release plus coordinated opposite-side withdrawal rather than completed-connector insertion or external-latch operation. The 5378 variant lacks acquired housing geometry, the generic nondestructive TE objective lacks an equipment-specific procedure, and cleaning-robot connector replacement lacks an OEM service procedure. Selection is for research and component-physics validation only: measured blade/tang geometry, forces, damage thresholds, YAM reachability, and full semantic novelty review remain mandatory before demo development or submission review.
